page: Vultr vbm-8c-132gb-v2 is a bare metal server belonging to the Bare Metal NVMe family. It is equipped with an Intel Xeon 2388G processor featuring 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs with a base clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The system includes 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, which translates to 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided by a 3840 GB NVMe SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. There are no GPUs configured on this instance.

In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates average CPU and database performance alongside strong single-threaded compression capabilities. The Intel Xeon CPU achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 2503.49 and a multi-core score of 20287.03. Gzip compression single-threaded throughput reached 36.27 GB/sec, and bzip3 decompression single-threaded throughput was 14.14 GB/sec, both of which are strong results. The Passmark memory score is in the top tier at 3390.33. However, uncached large-block memory bandwidth is a bottleneck, with read speeds of 36.93 GB/sec and write speeds of 19.38 GB/sec, both falling into the weak tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this bare metal server offers dedicated hardware resources and a high memory-to-core ratio of 1:8. This resource density is advantageous for workloads requiring direct hardware access without virtualization overhead. The primary tradeoff is the weak large-block memory bandwidth, which may limit performance in memory-intensive applications processing large datasets that exceed the CPU's 16 MB L3 cache.

This hardware configuration is appropriate for database hosting, static web serving, and memory-intensive workloads. The server achieved 16.84 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks and 12.59 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, indicating solid performance for web hosting and transactional database operations.
